items.notes: B021 strict-range PASS — Hays, Williamson, Bell. Diagnostic priority: Start with scale and the ligule. Lindheimer muhly is a large dense fountain-form bunchgrass, commonly around 1 m or more tall, with unusually long conspicuous membranous ligules and a tall feathery panicle. It dwarfs seep muhly and is completely unlike creeping nimblewill.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under user blanket approval on 2026-10-03.

items.notes: B021 strict-range PASS — Hays, Williamson, Travis. Diagnostic priority: Start with plant size and blade texture. Seep muhly is a compact upright bunchgrass, usually about 40–80 cm, with threadlike involute leaves and a delicate open panicle that often develops a reddish cast. It is much smaller than Lindheimer muhly but still truly tufted, unlike creeping nimblewill.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under user blanket approval on 2026-10-03.

items.notes: B021 strict-range PASS — Hays, Travis, Williamson. Diagnostic priority: Forget the ornamental-muhly silhouette: nimblewill is low and weak. Look for decumbent much-branched stems that root at the lower nodes, short flat blades, and a narrow contracted panicle. That creeping/rooting habit separates it instantly from the two upright bunchgrasses.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under user blanket approval on 2026-10-03.

items.notes: B022 PASS — Travis, Williamson, Kerr. Diagnostic priority: Start with flower size and the leaf node. Prairie penstemon has enormous pale lavender-to-white flowers, usually about 35–55 mm long, and opposite serrate stem leaves that are sessile and often fused across the node. The calyx and inflorescence are glandular-hairy, and the throat is abruptly inflated.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under user blanket approval through species-merge-029-penstemon-b022.

items.notes: B022 PASS — Hays, Kerr, Bandera. Diagnostic priority: Start with the glossy leaves and the narrower pink-to-red corolla. Hill Country penstemon is an erect perennial with opposite dark-green leaves; lower leaves are often toothed while upper leaves become smaller and more entire/connate. Flowers are usually about 25–35 mm, distinctly smaller than P. cobaea.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under user blanket approval through species-merge-029-penstemon-b022.

items.notes: B022 UNRESOLVED — Texas native, but fewer than 3 exact project target-zone counties verified. Diagnostic priority: Start with scale and habitat. Gulf Coast penstemon has much smaller lavender-to-violet flowers, about 10–14 mm long, on slender branched stems in wet alluvial or coastal-prairie settings. The calyx lobes are small and sharply pointed, and the exserted staminode carries orange hairs distally.
items.reconciliation_note: Texas-native status is accepted, but three exact project target-zone counties remain unverified; intentionally not installed.

items.notes: B022 PASS — Val Verde, Edwards, Bandera. Diagnostic priority: Start with the woody base and leaf texture. Rock penstemon is a low densely branched subshrub with thick dark-green leathery leaves that have coarse mucronate teeth. It grows from limestone cracks and carries red tubular flowers on short stalks.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under user blanket approval through species-merge-029-penstemon-b022.

items.notes: B025 PASS — Hays, Travis, Williamson. Diagnostic priority: Flip the leaf first. Mustang grape has a dense white-to-rusty woolly tomentum on the lower surface that essentially hides the blade surface and veins. Then confirm broad heart- to kidney-shaped leaves and large dark berries usually 12 mm or more.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under blanket approval through species-merge-031-vitis-b025.

items.notes: B025 PASS — Hays, Kerr, Bexar. Diagnostic priority: Start with the lower leaf surface and fruit bloom. Berlandier/Heller's grape has a lower leaf surface that remains visible—sparsely webby/hairy to nearly glabrous—not a solid white felt. Branchlets are slightly angled and usually lack red-banded nodes; ripe berries are conspicuously glaucous and the fruiting clusters are comparatively short and compact.
items.reconciliation_note: Old tracker Vitis cinerea var. helleri reconciled to current Kew accepted Vitis berlandieri; installed under blanket approval through species-merge-031-vitis-b025; aliases preserved.

items.notes: B025 UNRESOLVED — current taxon concept does not have 3 exact target-zone counties locked. Diagnostic priority: Treat this as a concept-check species. In the strict var. cinerea morphology, branchlets are distinctly angled and densely short-hairy plus cobwebby; leaf undersides stay visibly gray/green with both webby and short hairs, and berries are small and only slightly glaucous. Do not call a Central Texas Heller's grape V. cinerea solely because an app uses a broad species concept.

B025 UNRESOLVED — current taxon concept does not have 3 exact target-zone counties locked. Diagnostic priority: Look at the stem before the fruit. Catbird grape has uniformly red, purplish-red or chestnut branchlets and usually deeply 3(–5)-lobed leaves with long-pointed lobes. The lower leaf surface is essentially glabrous, and it is a riverbank/slough/floodplain grape.

B026 PASS — Hays, Travis, Williamson. Diagnostic priority: Start with where the flowers are. Common wild petunia sends a conspicuous peduncled, branching terminal flower stalk above the leaves; the flowers are not sitting directly in the leaf axils. Then confirm mostly glabrous/glabrescent oval-ovate leaves with wavy to low-dentate margins.
items.reconciliation_note: Tracker/familiar Ruellia nudiflora reconciled to current Kew accepted Ruellia ciliatiflora; old name preserved as alias; installed under blanket approval through species-merge-032-ruellia-b026.

items.notes: B026 PASS — Travis, Williamson, Real. Diagnostic priority: Look at the leaf axil. Drummond's ruellia has purple flowers/cymes essentially sessile in the axils rather than raised on a terminal stalk. The ovate leaves and stems have short fine pubescence, not the conspicuous long hairs of R. humilis. If fruit is present, the capsule's only 2–4 seeds are a powerful confirmation.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under blanket approval through species-merge-032-ruellia-b026.

items.notes: B026 PASS — Hays, Travis, Williamson. Diagnostic priority: Look for obvious individual hairs before looking at the flower. Prairie petunia is conspicuously long-pilose on stems, leaves and especially leaf margins, and its flowers are axillary and nearly sessile. That shaggy/ciliate look separates it from finely pubescent R. drummondiana and mostly glabrous terminal-flowered R. ciliatiflora.
items.reconciliation_note: Installed under blanket approval through species-merge-032-ruellia-b026.
